t: None of the funds made available in this Act may be used for a project or program named for an individual serving as a Member, Delegate, or Resident Commissioner of the United States House of Representatives.

fable.w: This is an appropriations restriction barring the use of funds for projects or programs named after sitting House Members. The tempting reading is that the mention of Members of Congress signals some interaction, but Congress is inside the federal government and no consultation, hearing, comment period, advisory body, or right to sue is created. No party outside the federal government is involved in any federal decision.

opus.w: This section only bars spending appropriated funds on projects named for sitting House members, Delegates or Resident Commissioners. It sets up no consultation, comment period, hearing, advisory body or right to sue. The mention of House members is not participation, because Congress is inside the federal government and they play no part in any decision here.
opus.b: 1. **Tempting-but-wrong reading:** The section names Members, Delegates and Resident Commissioners of the House. That might look like it involves outside parties. It doesn't: House members are part of Congress, which is inside the federal government. More importantly, the section sets up no process at all. It only bars spending funds on projects named after a sitting member.

qwen_chat.w: This section imposes a restriction on the use of federal funds regarding the naming of projects. It does not require or recommend any consultation, coordination, or input from parties outside the federal government. The prohibition is internal to the government's spending rules and does not involve an advisory board, public comment period, or consultation with states or the public.
qwen_chat.s: None of the funds made available in this Act may be used for a project or program named for an individual serving as a Member, Delegate, or Resident Commissioner of the United States House of Representatives.
qwen_chat.b: Tempting-but-wrong reading: One might argue that prohibiting naming projects after current members of Congress is a form of public participation because it involves the public (or at least non-federal entities) in the naming process by excluding certain names. However, this is a restriction on federal spending and naming conventions, not a mechanism for outside parties to consult with or influence a federal decision. There is no requirement for the government to seek input from the public, states, or other outside entities.
